task_row_model.query: For the planned randomized trial of Drug A versus placebo in essential hypertension, what are the required inclusion/exclusion criteria, the precise primary endpoint definition, the sample-size calculation parameters (including assumed effect size, SD, alpha, power, allocation, and total N), and the interim analysis rules?

documents.content: Protocol excerpt (academic style): Eligible participants are adults aged 18–75 with diagnosed essential hypertension and untreated clinic systolic blood pressure (SBP) 140–159 mmHg on two separate visits, each measured as the mean of two seated readings after 5 minutes rest. Participants must be off antihypertensive medications for at least four weeks. Exclusion criteria include secondary hypertension, estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <45 ml/min/1.73 m2, pregnancy or lactation, myocardial infarction within the prior six months, and uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c >9%). The trial’s primary endpoint is the change from baseline in clinic seated SBP at 12 weeks, calculated as the difference between mean-of-two readings at baseline and at week 12.
documents.reasoning_trace: Contains clinical eligibility criteria and the primary endpoint definition (measurement method and timing).

documents.content: Methods textbook fragment (statistical): For a two-arm, parallel randomized trial comparing mean systolic blood pressure change between groups, the investigators prespecified an effect size of 6 mmHg with an assumed common standard deviation of 12 mmHg. The sample-size calculation used a two-sided type I error alpha = 0.05 and power = 90% (beta = 0.10), with 1:1 allocation. Using the standard two-sample means formula yields approximately 85 participants per arm (total N ≈ 170) to detect the 6 mmHg difference under these assumptions. No planned blinded sample-size re-estimation is included.
documents.reasoning_trace: Provides statistical assumptions: delta, SD, alpha, power, allocation, and computed total sample size.

documents.content: Trial operations note (journalistic/report style): The study will include a single planned interim efficacy review when roughly half of the planned primary-endpoint data have accrued (≈50% of target N). An independent Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will conduct the unblinded review and may recommend stopping for overwhelming efficacy only. The trial uses an O'Brien–Fleming alpha-spending approach to preserve the overall two-sided 0.05 significance level. No interim futility stopping rule or sample-size reassessment is scheduled.
documents.reasoning_trace: Specifies timing and nature of the interim analysis, stopping criteria, alpha-spending method, and DSMB role.

documents.content: Background commentary (informal/speculative): Interest in Drug A stems from historical advances in antihypertensive classes such as ACE inhibitors and diuretics; blog-style notes discuss ambulatory versus clinic BP measurement and cite unrelated case reports of atypical responders. Several paragraphs muse about long-term cardiovascular outcomes and public-health implications of modest BP reductions, and include redundant definitions of hypertension stages, but do not alter the trial's primary design parameters.

task_row_model.golden_answer: Include adults 18–75 with essential hypertension, untreated clinic SBP 140–159 mmHg on two visits (mean of two seated readings), off antihypertensives ≥4 weeks. Exclude secondary hypertension, eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73 m2, pregnancy/lactation, MI within 6 months, or HbA1c >9%. Primary endpoint: change in mean seated SBP at 12 weeks. Sample-size assumptions: delta=6 mmHg, SD=12, two-sided alpha=0.05, power=90%, 1:1 allocation, total N ≈170 (≈85/arm). One interim at 50% accrual with O'Brien–Fleming alpha-spending; DSMB may stop for efficacy only; no sample-size re-estimation.
